title: AES-GCM ivSz not constrained to 12 bytes
description:
crypto2dev_cipher() takes ivSz from info->cipher.aesgcm_enc.ivSz (line 607) and only validates ivSz > CRYPTO2DEV_IV_MAXLEN (32). It does not verify ivSz == 12.

AES-GCM is defined for 96-bit (12-byte) nonces per NIST SP 800-38D. wolfSSL may pass non-12-byte nonces under some configurations (e.g., TLS 1.2 explicit IV, or direct API use).

Trigger: wc_AesGcmEncrypt/Decrypt called with ivSz != 12.
Outcome: depends on kernel driver. The driver may accept the wrong-length nonce silently (producing ciphertext/tag computed under a non-standard IV derivation) or reject with EINVAL (→ WC_HW_E). In the acceptance case there is no error signal — the caller gets wrong authentication.

Fix: add 'if (info->cipher.type == WC_CIPHER_AES_GCM && ivSz != GCM_NONCE_MID_SZ) return BAD_FUNC_ARG;' after the cipher switch block (GCM_NONCE_MID_SZ = 12).
